rows.doc: The market fee: this share of each fill, from the seller, rounded up (GDD 10.2).
A craft or a milestone pick costs this per station tier (GDD 6).
A made kind is worth its inputs plus this a step (GDD 10.10).
What a faction order pays for one provision.
What a settlement's market asks for one provision.
Repair costs this per durability point restored (GDD 6).
What a stable asks for a mount, per tier.
Faction buying per active character per world day, world-wide, at rest (GDD 10.2). Tuned by the Economy run so the band holds across population sizes.
Active characters each open settlement's faction orders assume besides those trading there, so a new world, and a settlement nobody plays from, still has buyers.
The stabiliser's band: coin per active character below this raises the faucet (GDD 10.5).
Above this lowers it.
How far the faucet moves a world day outside the band.
Inside the band, the faucet moves this share of itself back toward faucet-rate each world day.
The window coin per active character is averaged over.

The stabiliser never raises the faucet past this share of faucet-rate, and passes faucet-rate itself only while coin per active character is not already climbing: a small server short of coin drifts up to the band, a large one filling new purses does not overshoot it.
A character is active if it acted within this many world days (GDD 10.2).
A market order or listing lasts this long (GDD 10.3).
Open orders, listings and gear buy orders a character may hold at once.
A faction order's price at the most urgent need, against reference (GDD 10.4); no need is 100.
Added to the urgency of blade orders from a faction at war.
Coin sold to a faction for each standing gained with it (GDD 5.4).
A character younger than this is capped on what it gives away (GDD 10.9).
What a young character may give away a world day, coin and goods at reference value.
World days of price history a book keeps.
A ledger report is posted every this many world days (GDD 10.5).
The goal listing fee, a share of the reward (GDD 10.2).
The least a goal listing pays.
What a settlement's trader pays for an item, against its value (GDD 4.18).
What the trader lists an item it bought at, against its value.
A trader's fortune rises or falls in steps of this much coin in its purse, each a fact.
World hours of a world day a character acting in at least this many is flagged for review (GDD 10.9).
World days in a row the cadence must hold before the flag.
Trades a settlement's market forum post names a world day (GDD 17.2).
Cover at or above this raises a tile's ambush chance one band (GDD 10.7).
Share of each settlement's faucet budget its trader may spend buying items a world day.
